payload.name: AddNewMemoryWhenNoExistingMatch
payload.description: When a candidate contains new, evidence-backed information and no existing memory is retrieved for merging, use ADD rather than SKIP.
content: During CRUD decisions, if no existing memory matches a candidate, do not skip it for that reason; issue an ADD operation to create a new memory.
Before deciding SKIP, confirm the candidate is redundant or unsupported; lack of an update/merge target alone is not a valid skip reason.
This applies to the CRUD decision stage; extraction should still produce candidates for all new facts regardless of existing memory.

solves: This addresses the pattern where a new, evidence-backed fact is dropped during CRUD because no existing memory matches. The rule applies to any candidate representing new information; it does not apply when the candidate is redundant, unsupported, or outside the allowed memory kinds.
